$comment: Roll XI content target. This file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for what the finished dataset should contain. It declares scope as RULES, not as an enumerated list of teams. scripts/coverage.mjs diffs this against the actual packs in public/data/ and prints the remaining gap. Do not hand-edit progress into this file: progress is derived. Only edit this file to change the GOAL.

stageCodes.MAIN: Main draw participant, round unknown or not applicable

roles.roster: Club-season has a full player list. Draftable in Campaign, appears in Daily, Album and Chains.
roles.stub: Club-season has rating + kit + scorer names only. Usable as Campaign opposition. No players, so it does not appear in Daily, Album or Chains.
roles.$note: A club-season may need BOTH: rosters are drafted by the player, stubs are faced as opposition. See docs/CONTENT-TARGET.md section 3 for why these are no longer mutually exclusive.

scopes.$note: Decided 2026-08-07: pre-1995 International Football Cup is OUT OF SCOPE permanently. Scope begins at the UEFA-run era, 1995. Format note: no separate qualifying tier to exclude 1995-2005 (see top-level mainDrawDefinition.perCompetitionNotes.ITC); 2006-2008 used 11 parallel mini-tournaments with no runner-up designation.

mainDrawDefinition.rule: Main draw = group/round-robin phase participants only. Qualifying and preliminary rounds are OUT OF SCOPE for every competition, in every era.

perCompetitionNotes.EC: 1955-56 to 1991-92 had no group stage; it was a straight knockout. For these editions 'main draw' means Round 1 proper. A small number of early editions ran a preliminary round for lower-ranked federations before Round 1 — that preliminary round is excluded. Needs per-edition verification; do not assume Round 1 fields are uniform in size.
perCompetitionNotes.UCL: 1992-93 to 2023-24: group stage participants, i.e. teams that survived qualifying and were drawn into the eight (later four) groups. 2024-25 onward: league-phase participants (36 teams), which plays the same structural role as the old group stage. Qualifying-round-only exits are excluded even if the club is well known.
perCompetitionNotes.CWC: Straight knockout throughout its history (1960-61 to 1998-99), same treatment as pre-1992 EC: 'main draw' means Round 1 proper, excluding any preliminary round used for smaller federations in some seasons.
perCompetitionNotes.FAIRS: Straight knockout, city-based entry in its earliest editions. 'Main draw' means Round 1 proper. Entry format was irregular in 1955-58 and 1958-60 (multi-year, small field) — verify per edition rather than assuming a standard bracket size.
perCompetitionNotes.UEFA: 1971-72 to 2003-04: straight knockout, some editions had a qualifying round for clubs from lower-ranked federations — excluded. 2004-05 to 2008-09: the competition added a group stage; 'main draw' for these five editions means the group stage, not the preceding knockout qualifying rounds.
perCompetitionNotes.UEL: Group stage participants throughout (2009-10 onward), excluding all qualifying and play-off rounds. From 2024-25 this becomes the 36-team league phase.
perCompetitionNotes.CONFL: Group stage participants, excluding qualifying and play-off rounds, all editions (2021-22 onward).
perCompetitionNotes.ITC: The Intertoto Cup ran its own round-robin group phase directly (no separate qualifying tier to exclude) from 1995 through 2005, so 'main draw' there is simply every group entrant. 2006-2008 changed format entirely to 11 parallel single-elimination mini-tournaments with no group phase; treat every entrant to those mini-tournaments as main draw for those three years.

competitionCodes.$note: CANONICAL codes. The dataset currently uses two spellings for two competitions. Normalise on these and delete the aliases.

packGranularity.rationale: The existing C-series (Serie A, one pack per season, ~90-100 rows) and the C10-C14 five-season batch experiment (same source method, larger files) are the two data points this project actually has for accuracy vs. build effort. Both sit in the 80-120 club-season range per pack without a documented quality problem. Editions-per-pack is the wrong unit to standardise on, because edition size varies hugely by competition: a UEFA Cup Round 1 alone can carry 60-80 club-seasons, while an early Fairs Cup or Conference League edition carries a dozen. Fixing 'one pack per edition' would produce wildly uneven, sometimes huge, files for the high-participant competitions. Fixing 'five editions per pack' (literally copying the Serie A batch size) would do the same in reverse for those same competitions. Target the row count instead and let edition-count-per-pack float to hit it.
rules: One pack = one competition (or one league) and one contiguous span of seasons. Never mix competitions or leagues in a pack.
For low-density competitions (Fairs Cup, Conference League, Intertoto, early EC/CWC), batch multiple whole editions per pack until the target row count is reached.

For high-density competitions (UEFA Cup Round 1, modern UCL/UEL/CONFL group-league phase), one edition may already meet or exceed the target on its own — do not force multiple editions into one file if it pushes the pack past ~150-200 rows.
Never split a single edition's main draw across two packs. The unit that must stay atomic is the edition, not the pack.

Serie A keeps its proven per-season pack size (~18-20 rows) rather than being forced into strict decade boundaries — a literal 'one pack per decade' would produce 180-200-row files for post-war decades, above the target band. Organise Serie A packs as decade-labelled BATCHES of the existing per-season build (e.g. a 1930s batch built and shipped as 3-4 packs of ~5 seasons each, matching the C10-C14 precedent), so 'by decade' survives as a navigational grouping in index.json without forcing oversized files.
